name: Day Hike - Diorite Falls - Paluma NP
description:
Sunday 26th March, 2023
 
Day Hike - Diorite Falls - Paluma NP
 
Leader: Ian Wallace 
 
Rated: Easy to Medium. Consider the distance involved in your decision making. The pace will be moderate and steady, so we can cover the distance within the designated time-frame and enjoy our stops at the points of interest mentioned above. 
 
Description: 
Beginning at the Paluma Dam campground, we’ll head north along the dam wall and then through the rainforest to the Diorite Falls. We’ll spend some time there, so there will be an opportunity for a swim and a look around – I reckon it should be looking pretty good after recent rainfall. After that we’ll take a different trail back to the Paluma Dam campground, basically we'll be doing an extended clockwise circuit around the dam.

What to expect:
-Creek crossings and rock hopping
-The terrain is undulating with some steep sections
-We make a gradual descent to Diorite Falls, and the ascent on the return journey involves a lot of uphill including one section which is around 1km of constant uphill.

Approximate: -Distance: 18-20kms  Duration: 6-7 hours including stops & breaks

Meeting Point -
The dirt carpark next to BP Service station, Yabulu (Ingham direction) at 6:00am – From here we’ll carpool to the start point of the hike at the Paluma Dam.
Or Paluma Dam at 7:15 ish

What to bring:
-Water: 3-4 litres recommended. Sterilisation tablets if you plan to refill your water supply from creeks
-Shoes appropriate for walking on rocky, uneven surfaces. Acceptance that you will be walking in wet shoes as we will be crossing some creeks.
-Dry clothes and maybe thongs for after the walk
-Trail snacks, morning tea and lunch
-First-aid kit and snake bite bandage
Register - Diorite Falls 
Must be over 18yrs to participate.   

If conditions on the day are unsuitable then the route and walk length may be changed at the leader’s discretion. 
 
Please Note - If you are a new walker/non-member who has not walked with us before – please contact the walk leader before RSVP registration. Email Ian at - ian.wallace@westnet.com.au  Or call him -  0404509282. 

Fee: non-members/visitors/-  $5 . TBWC Club members - Free. 
You can become a TBWC member after 3 walks as a visitor

For more info, contact the leader - Ian at ian.wallace@westnet.com.au


To register for the walk, Please use the form below. 
https://forms.gle/y3xJJ4SnU5RDtvgcA

For Club Members – if the RSVP registration is fully subscribed, contact the leader direct to discuss participation.

name: Waterfall Way
description:
Next bushwalk - Waterfall Way in Wooroonooran National Park

An off-track remote wilderness adventure.
Continuing our recent theme of off-track wilderness exploring, Saturday and Sunday we will follow an old overgrown logging road to this hidden area.
Duration - Two days
Require camping gear
Rated - Hard.
Pre-Registration / approval with the walk leader is essential. Register ASAP to reserve a spot.
For more info, contact the club info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.com
Leader: Luen Warneke 
Meet: 6:00am - ask the walk leader for the location once registered. IT IS MANDORTORY TO CORRESPOND WITH THE LEADER.
REGISTER: https://forms.gle/tiwL8y4frBHBCQSLA

Secateurs are mandatory!!!

This is a remote rainforest bushwalk. There will be crossing creeks (so walking in the water), slippery rocks and roots, uneven footing, tangled vines, LOTS of wait-a-while and gimpie gimpie, all that good fun adventure. The rewards is the best waterfall in Far North Queensland,  great scenery, adventure, a sense of achievement, and great company. See photos on the club's Facebook or Luen's website wanderstories.space for examples of potential bushwalking conditions from the recent creek based exploratory adventures.

The walk leader will send out a brief hike description and route plan prior to the walk. 

Fully two days hike, anticipate back at the cars around 5 pm Sunday depending on water conditions and group , etc.
Wear appropriate footwear, i.e., enclosed sturdy shoes that grip on slippery rocks.
Drinking water - carry 2+ lt, refill from creeks as required (but suitably treat/filter any water refills from natural sources, or carry 3+ lt). The club also recommends use of electrolytes during the day.
Bring food and snacks to suits your energy needs for the bushwalking and camping.
Bushwalkers should bring their own personal (minimal) first aid kit, headtorch, and whistle, etc. 
Own camping gear, etc.
Luen will also have his personal minimal first aid kit and PLB. The club does not provide a group first aid kit.
Fees: non-members $5
Clothing - as it off-track bushwalking, long sleeve clothing or gaiters is recommended. Otherwise you will have cuts/scratches on exposed skin at the end of the day.
Must be over 18yrs to participate.
Email - info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.com
